title: Roosevelt Grill house band with Jack Lesberg
summary: At Gibson's Roosevelt Grill, Leeman and Lesberg are the house rhythm section behind Joe Venuti, Buck Clayton and Peanuts Hucko, and later back Bobby Hackett.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: years, that I just can't put my finger on many of them without research. Until we came to the point of Dick Gibson, and his World's Greatest Jazz Band, and he opened into the Roosevelt Grill in New York, and had a music policy there. That's another one of his wonderful promotions for jazz music.

I worked there with Jack Lesberg. He and I -- he was bass drummer and I was the house drummer, and we worked there with such groups as Joe Venuti as a leader for awhile, and Buck Clayton a couple of times, and we had Peanuts Hucko for a leader -- we were what you called the intermission band, I guess. While the World's Greatest Jazz Band took time off.

I'll get to the time that I was there with Bobby Hackett because we made five or six albums while playing live from there. One of the greatest albums I ever made in my own personal taste, was the last album. The sound and the soloist and he fours that I took, and so forth, were to me, the best -- the epitome of my playing, if I may say -- for my liking, the band was Dave McKenna on piano, Jack Lesberg on bass, Bobby Hackett and he made it a co-feature with Bobby Hackett, featuring Vic Dickenson.
